highlights.title: Mister Organ is one of the most unsettling documentaries I’ve ever seen
highlights.summary: Mister Organ doesn't reach the level of societal horror of The Act of Killing or the creepypasta-meets-true-crime gruesomeness of Beware the Slenderman, but there's something deeply unsettling about Michael Organ and his intimate campaign of terror against everyone who enters his life.
body: The story of Michael Organ is the rare documentary that doubles as a psychological horror film.

Mister Organ is a documentary by David Farrier, an Auckland, New Zealand journalist. The movie starts with Farrier reporting on Bashford Antiques, a shop in Ponsonby that has begun aggressively clamping cars in its lot and demanding exorbitant fees to release them — up to $760. Farrier’s article for The Spinoff eventually led the government to introduce legislation that would outlaw extreme clamping fees.
Under normal circumstances, that would be the end of the story. But at the center of this story is a man named Michael Organ who turns out to be a bizarre, seemingly dangerous conman.

Organ was hired to police Bashford’s lot, and during his investigation, Farrier discovers he’s more than just a parking-lot bully. Years earlier, Organ had been charged with attempting to steal a yacht in an elaborate scheme. What’s more, he claimed to be a prince and a lawyer — he is neither.

highlights.title: Taika Waititi Says His Star Wars Movie Is 'on Ice'
highlights.summary: Director Taika Waititi has confirmed his long-in-development Star Wars movie is officially "on ice." The Thor: Ragnarok and Jojo Rabbit filmmaker provided Inverse with the update when speaking to the outlet during a press junket for his new film, Klara and the Sun.
body: "I hate to break this to you, but we're going to actually put it on ice and we're working on a different thing together," he said.

Brutal. Rumors that Disney and Lucasfilm had approached the What We Do in the Shadows filmmaker to helm a Star Wars project go as far back as January 2020. That's just a few years after he took off as the mastermind behind one of the most beloved Marvel Cinematic Universe movies to date, with an official announcement confirming he was attached to a movie arriving just a few months later.

It was mostly good news at first. In 2021, Waititi said he had finished his Star Wars movie's story, and in 2022, then-Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy said the goal was to bring it to theaters in late 2023. At the time, she also admitted that Disney hadn't "locked anything in" quite yet, a fact that only became more apparent in the years that followed.

highlights.summary: Arsenal's only shot on target proved enough to snatch victory at Nottingham Forest through Noni Madueke's deflected strike, keeping the champions within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City and condemning Forest to the relegation zone.
body: After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. Murillo almost salvaged a point in stoppage time with a superb solo run, driving at the Arsenal defence before curling narrowly wide. Ezri Konsa then made a crucial late challenge to deny Liam Delap.
However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.

highlights.summary: Sharing food with others begets a certain type of magic. That goes double for baked goods and desserts. In The Witch’s Bakery, that magic is literal. It’s a charming, cozy, and heartfelt adventure that goes heavy on the Studio Ghibli vibes.
body: In Sunny Lab’s debut game, you play as the heart witch Lunne who moves to Paris and sets up a magical bake shop, along with her pink, cat-like companion Orio. Monday through Saturday, her days are consumed by work. Prepare dough, infuse it with magic, and have Orio bake it with their elemental magic. Tend to customers and rake in that dough. Er, dough being money, in this case.

Some customers are indecisive, while others are impatient. Anyone who’s worked in food service or retail will, unfortunately, not be surprised by the annoyances of those customers. Where Lune’s magic comes into play is for customers haunted by regrets that manifest as cute creatures floating around them, which only the magically inclined can see.

highlights.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.summary: Anthropic has granted external evaluators “employee-like access” to assess the risks of its models, following through on a commitment to increase safeguards over concerns the technology could run catastrophically out of control.
body: METR, a nonprofit that has worked with leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office with access to its hardware and internal systems.

A greater role for third-party evaluators is among the main concrete steps the labs have proposed in response to rising concern about the dangers more capable AI systems could pose to the economy, cyber security and humanity at large.

Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei achieved a rare moment of unity with arch-rivals Sam Altman and Elon Musk in September when the OpenAI and SpaceX bosses rallied behind his proposal to embed external auditors in the leading labs.
Thursday’s announcement marks the first step to implementing these pledges. OpenAI has yet to lay out plans to bring in evaluators after Altman said Amodei’s proposals were a good idea.

highlights.title: Giving AI a “crystal clear” view of the materials world
highlights.summary: New research can help AI models understand crystalline materials in 3D and reason about their properties.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."

In principle, artificial intelligence could make finding the right material for an application as simple as ordering dinner: Scientists would tell a large language model what they want, and it would serve them a perfectly designed crystal for the job.

Unfortunately, that approach doesn’t work well yet, and the problem comes down to data: Most materials consist of crystals, which are 3D periodic arrangements of atoms whose structures are stored in specialized formats, not the text streams that today’s large language models are trained on. The experimental literature is also heavily biased toward a few popular classes of crystals, making AI outputs skew toward those materials.

highlights.title: Silent Hill Remake Studio Wants to Make Physical Games 'for as Long as Possible'
highlights.summary: Silent Hill developer Bloober Team wants to make physical versions of its games "for as long as possible." Studio CEO Piotr Babieno opened up about the company's appreciation for physical media and collectibles during an interview with GamesRadar.
body: "Like, OK, the game can have a slightly higher resolution and maybe better lighting and whatever, but will it make it a more engaging game? I don't think so," Babieno said.

The CEO for the studio behind the Silent Hill 2 remake and its in-development original Silent Hill remake also talked about how stats show "the majority of players are playing on hardware which is five, seven years old, if not older." He continued, saying, "But are they less interested in games because of that? I don't think so."

As AI shapes a new, controversial future in the gaming industry, the Bloober executive seems to be more interested in "thinking about other senses." It's this mindset that the team has carried into its new Nintendo Switch 2-exclusive 2.5D horror game, Onyx: The Dark Group. For this experience, which comes from Bloober subsidiary Broken Mirror Games, it's become about "putting horror back in your hands."

"As humans, we have four other senses, and AI can deliver something for what you see, for what you hear, but why not touch?" Babieno said. "I think the physical element of gaming will always, always be there."

highlights.title: Julianne Moore Says ‘The Debut’ Is ‘One of the Best Scripts I’ve Ever Read’ as Jesse Eisenberg’s Musical Comedy Closes London Film Festival on a High Note
highlights.summary: “The Debut” ended London Film Festival on a high note Sunday night as director Jesse Eisenberg and star Julianne Moore gushed over each other to a packed audience at the Royal Festival Hall.
body: “I mean, this movie stars my favorite person, Julianne Moore,” Eisenberg began as the duo came onstage to introduce the musical comedy. “But ironically, strangely, it’s the story of my life.”
Moore, wearing a chic black gown, returned the praise. She called “The Debut” an “incredible gift” and said it’s “one of the best scripts I’ve ever read in my entire life.”

“It was such an honor to receive it and such a thrill to go to work every day and to get to do this incredible part with these tremendous actors,” she said, adding of Eisenberg: “He’s a beautiful writer, exemplary director and just a great talent.”
In response, Eisenberg quipped: “I just want to note that the only time I’m called beautiful, it’s about writing.”

highlights.title: CBS's Definitive '80s Action Thriller Series Is Officially Free to Watch on Streaming
highlights.summary: Premiering on CBS in 1984, Airwolf starred Jan-Michael Vincent as Hawke, a brooding Vietnam veteran and test pilot who takes possession of a top-secret military helicopter.
body: The 1980s were a golden age for television action heroes and their ridiculously cool rides. Michael Knight had a talking Pontiac Trans Am. The A-Team had its customized van. But Stringfellow Hawke? He had a supersonic helicopter armed to the teeth, capable of outrunning fighter jets and turning virtually any type of enemy aircraft into scrap metal. Throw in a secret hideaway inside a mountain and one of television's catchiest theme songs, and Airwolf was practically irresistible to anyone who grew up watching '80s television.

Now streaming for free on The Roku Channel, Airwolf is a reminder of just how much fun '80s action television could be. Unlike Magnum, P.I. or The A-Team, however, its biggest star wasn't one of the actors. It was the helicopter, and nearly four decades after the series ended, it's still one of television's most memorable machines.
points: Premiering on CBS in 1984, Airwolf starred Jan-Michael Vincent as Hawke, a brooding Vietnam veteran and test pilot who takes possession of a top-secret military helicopter.
The 1980s were a golden age for television action heroes and their ridiculously cool rides.
Throw in a secret hideaway inside a mountain and one of television's catchiest theme songs, and Airwolf was practically irresistible to anyone who grew up watching '80s television.

highlights.title: The Most Evocative Period Dramas of the 21st Century
highlights.summary: The best period dramas whisk viewers to times and places that feel a world away from modern life. Here are our favorites, from “Gosford Park” to “The Crown.”
body: Sumptuous costume dramas can provide a much-needed escape in troubling times, but if you’re tired of the usual assortment of airless parlors, manicured lawns, and straight-laced suitors, there is an alternative: a subset of recent films and series that play with our expectations of the genre. Combining post-punk soundtracks with cross-dressing, lobster racing, color-blind casting, and illicit love affairs, they allow us to view history through a new lens and feel surprisingly modern as a result. See our favorites below.

You can rely on Armando Iannucci to breathe new life into Charles Dickens’s sprawling bildungsroman. In the hands of the endlessly inventive comedian, the tale of a boy who pulls himself up by his bootstraps and seeks out fame and fortune becomes a madcap delight complete with a zingy script, cartoonish punch-ups, collapsing sets, and a heady dose of magical realism. Dev Patel is the dashing lead, supported by Peter Capaldi as a top-hatted menace and Tilda Swinton as an eccentric landowner who kicks trespassers off their donkeys.

highlights.title: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
highlights.summary: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years ago. A few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about.
body: You could say that I fell down a Wiki rabbit hole, especially when it came to the website’s early years. Almost everything important about the project came together quite quickly. Its amateurish, homegrown ethos was off-putting to a lot of writers and journalists, and that meant many questions about why it had worked had no answers. Most of the people seriously interested in Wikipedia were a handful of academics – so I decided to write a book about it.

Because Wikipedia is so massive, writing an “exhaustive” book on it is impossible, like trying to represent a mountain with a grain of sand. Instead, I concentrated on the human history – the small, sometimes very small, number of people who really influenced what Wikipedia became. Wikipedians can be difficult, and the most ornery get a bad wrap – even the Wikimedia Foundation’s leadership has made comments about their “Dorito-stained fingers”, or tendency to stay home on a Saturday night. But by the end of the process, I was in awe of them, and I still am.

Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page: … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages…
body: Language that experts say allowed the scraping of news sites to train its AI has been removed from Meta’s terms.

Many, including Neiman Lab and James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, interpreted it as an attempt to give Meta the right to use content scraped from sites to train its AI products for free and supersede blocking instructions in a site’s robots.txt file.

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers. As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”

highlights.title: Street Fighter Tops the Box Office With $51 Million Opening Weekend Amid Lackluster Reviews
highlights.summary: Capcom's Street Fighter movie spun up $51.1 million in its opening weekend, securing its place atop the global box office despite some not-so-great reviews.
body: Ryu (Andrew Koji), Ken (Noah Centineo), and the rest of the film's massive cast grappled with an estimated $31 million domestically and $20.1 million internationally in its theatrical debut. That's a figure that landed it a comfortable first place worldwide, even if it's not a perfect victory across the board.

As audiences turned up for performances – including Callina Liang's Chun-Li, David Dastmalchian's M. Bison, and Jason Momoa's Blanka – not everyone was so happy with how director Kitao Sakurai brought Capcom's classic fighting game franchise to the big screen. In its first few days in the public's gaze, Street Fighter has amassed a critics' score of 44 on IMDb and 41% on Rotten Tomatoes. IGN gave it a 6/10.

That's serviceable as far as gaming adaptations go and sub-par in the grand scheme. Generally, fans are feeling pretty positive about what they've seen thanks to some crisp animation and fight sequences. " Dumb fun " is one phrase floating around for the film, which doesn't seem to be for everyone but has still pulled in 79% positivity from audiences, according to Rotten Tomatoes.

highlights.title: There are five signs that someone dislikes you – but it’s best to ignore them | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: All the possible indications, from eye contact to body language, come with a disclaimer. The truth is, you can never be totally sure... I’d be far less paranoid if everyone wasn’t out to get me, so when BBC Science Focus dangled “ The subtle signs somebody secretly dislikes you ”, I’ve never…
body: The first indication? They avoid eye contact. Apparently “someone who repeatedly looks away, scans the room or avoids mutual gaze might be creating psychological distance”. Agreed. But they may also be checking to see who else arrives, which might not mean they secretly hate you, only that they secretly don’t like you as much as whoever just came in.

The second sign is unarguably more convincing. “Their facial expressions show contempt or disgust.” Admittedly, I’m no psychologist, but still, if someone looked contemptuous or disgusted while interacting with me, I’d be pretty confident in concluding that they aren’t my greatest fan all on my own. File this one under bear/woods, pope/Catholic.

Third up, they “smile less around you”. This feels dangerous, because the only way to know whether they are smiling less around you than other humans they come into contact with is to put them under surveillance and keep a tally. If they didn’t dislike you before you hid in a bush counting their grins, they probably would afterwards.

highlights.title: What are self-replicating ‘AI worms’, and why is Anthropic worried about them?
highlights.summary: The tech company says successful AI worms need more capability on less powerful devices, but current trends make that feasible by the end of the year. Warnings about what artificial intelligence might do in the future – together with alarming reports of what it has gotten up to already – are being…
body: Yet a report this week from Anthropic’s offensive research team grabbed attention by describing a new, practical threat, one devoid of human characteristics or apocalyptic musings. The red team, as such internal testers are called, said it created a malicious AI program that spread autonomously through internet-connected “smart” televisions and could do the same inside other ordinary devices. While machines running AI usually need a fair amount of computing power, the researchers said that their program split parts of itself among 15 televisions and was still able to function by using a bit of power from each.

In addition to evoking the horcruxes that kept pieces of Lord Voldemort’s soul alive within objects in the Harry Potter series, the report alarmed some professionals because the generally weak security of smart televisions and many other “internet of things” devices would be very hard to correct, even with a concerted effort.

highlights.title: 36 Years Later, Robert De Niro's Greatest Gangster Movie Quote Is Still One of a Kind
highlights.summary: Few actors have done more to shape the modern cinematic gangster than Robert De Niro. Across decades of mob dramas, he's played men who command respect through intimidation, calculation, and a religious devotion to the rules of their world.
body: Through all these roles, De Niro has delivered plenty of unforgettable lines, but one of his most memorable isn't a threat or a declaration of power. It's a deceptively simple piece of advice, one that succinctly sums up the gangster mentality built on loyalty. Ripped from Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas (based on Nicholas Pilegg's non-fiction crime chronicle Wiseguy ), De Niro’s James “Jimmy” Conway offers the following sage advice: "Never rat on your friends and always keep your mouth shut."

The line comes after a young Henry Hill (Ray Liotta) refuses to talk following a bust for selling untaxed cigarettes, earning his stripes by making it through his first court appearance without informing on any of his accomplices. Outside the courtroom, Conway slips him a handful of cash and congratulates him on surviving his first pinch. Then he pulls Henry close and imparts the cardinal rules of their world, turning a low-level arrest into a defining rite of passage for a kid desperate to prove his place in the organization.
points: Few actors have done more to shape the modern cinematic gangster than Robert De Niro.

highlights.title: Stars Kept the Night Going at Giorgio Armani’s Academy Gala After-Party at Chateau Marmont
highlights.summary: Right at the 10:30 p.m. kickoff, a flurry of camera flashes turned the sidewalk into a makeshift red carpet as paparazzi lined the street, eager to capture the industry’s brightest stars making their entrances.
body: With its storied charm, intimate atmosphere, and softly lit interiors, any night at Chateau Marmont is guaranteed to be a memorable one. Add a guest list overflowing with Hollywood crème de la crème to the mix and that magic is amplified tenfold. That was certainly true on Saturday night, when top-of-the-call-sheet names descended on the historic hotel for Giorgio Armani’s second annual Academy Museum Gala after-party.

Tracee Ellis Ross rolled in, nearly impossible to miss in her tangerine-hued, fringe-and-bead-adorned number from Balenciaga’s spring 2027 runway. She soon traded her barely-there, transparent high heels for white glove-style ballet flats in a practical fashion move. Others, however, tried to fly under the radar. Case in point: pals Leonardo DiCaprio and Tobey Maguire darted inside, heads down with their baseball caps pulled low.

The bash also doubled as a mini reunion for some. Shortly after arriving, Zoey Deutch caught the eye of Colman Domingo. “Zoey!” the actor exclaimed as he spotted her and pulled her close for a warm hug. Kate Hudson, who had swapped her earlier custom Armani Privé gown for a dramatic black feathered confection, soon joined the conversation.
